rows.english: It's easy to see how you would prove someone wrong if they replied, "It doesn't necessarily follow." Suppose though you say, It's not correct [to say that we have to draw a distinction between the "group" in the "group of similar cases in a proof that sounds are changing things" and being part of the group of similar cases in the same proof]. It is so correct to say this, because there are three different things that the word chok can make you think of--there are three different things that the word chok can refer to--when we speak of the "chok" in a proof that sounds are changing things. The chok in the word chokchu ("relationship between the subject and the reason") refers to the subject in the particular logical statement: the thing which the opponent doubts possesses the quality to be proven. Then there are pair of further uses of this word: the chok we use when we are discussing whether or not something is part of the group of similar cases (tunchok), and the chok we use when we are discussing the object related to, within the necessary relationships in a logical statement (kyappay drelyul gyi chok). Both of these refer to the general type represented by the quality to be proven, or--in this case--the general type represented by "changing thing." Finally there is the word chok as we use it in the expression "group of similar cases" (tunchok) itself. Here the word must be understood as referring to everything: to both the general type and the specific instance represented

[Translator's note: The DGA' GZHI in all manuscripts available to us is a miscarving for DGA\" BZHI; see S5313, f. 3b.  The reference here is also corrupted in all available manuscripts; it should read (as per the same text and folio), MAS BRTAN LAS LANGS PA'I YAS BABS KYI BZHI NI, SNGA MA'I MAS BRTAN LAS BDE BA CHE ZHING,]"}

rows.acip: DBANG BZHI THOB PA NI SMIN LAM DU 'JUG ZIN PAS NA 'JUG RUNG DU MI 'GRO BA'I PHYIR DE LTAR BZHAG PA MI 'THAD PAR STAG PHU BSTAN PA'I RGYAL MTSAN SOGS RANG PHYOGS KYI MKHAS GRUB TSAD LDAN MANG POS GSUNGS PAS, 'DIR RANG LUGS GONG DU BSHAD PA LTAR SMIN LAM 'JUG RUNG DBANG BZHI MA THOB BA NYID LA 'JOG DGOS,
rows.wylie: dbang bzhi thob pa ni smin lam du 'jug zin pas na 'jug rung du mi 'gro ba'i phyir de ltar bzhag pa mi 'thad par stag phu bstan pa'i rgyal mtshan sogs rang phyogs kyi mkhas grub tshad ldan mang pos gsungs pas, 'dir rang lugs gong du bshad pa ltar smin lam 'jug rung dbang bzhi ma thob ba nyid la 'jog dgos
rows.english: The fact is though that, once one receives the four empowerments, they have already entered the path that ripens us, so you can't say that they have made them fit to enter it.  Asserting that they do is incorrect, as many unerring and accomplished masters of our own school, such as Tenpay Gyeltsen of Takpu and others, have stated.  Therefore on this question we must adhere to the position we stated above, and establish a person as being fit to enter the path that ripens only if they have not received the four empowerments.

rows.acip: CES SRUNG 'KHOR BSGOM, MTSAMS 'OG TU 'JOG DGOS RIGS MTSAMS 'DIR SRUNG 'KHOR GYI NANG DU YOD PA'I MOS PA DANG BCAS DE DAG MI BRJED PA'I BRDAR MING BYANG LA RDE'U RE BSGRIL TE 'DREN PA'AM YID BSHAR BYED,
rows.wylie: ces srung 'khor bsgom, mtshams 'og tu 'jog dgos rigs mtshams 'dir srung 'khor gyi nang du yod pa'i mos pa dang bcas de dag mi brjed pa'i brdar ming byang la rde'u re bsgril te 'dren pa'am yid bshar byed
rows.english: With this we are picturing the protection circles.  Believe now that all of the people who are allowed to come within the boundaries of your retreat are there with you.  As a token to remind you of who they are, you should have a little slip of paper with a pebble for each person wrapped within it; or you can just review who they are in your mind. Blessing Our Meditation Seat

rows.acip: DA DUNG NAN TAN BYED NA MTSAMS 'OG TU 'JOG DGOS RNAMS KYI MING BRI BA'AM, YANG NA RDE'U RE LA MING RE BRIS TE DE DANG DE YIN BSAM, DE THOG MING MI GSAL BA'I RDE'U LNGA DRUG SOGS GANG DGOS BZHAG STE
rows.wylie: da dung nan tan byed na mtshams 'og tu 'jog dgos rnams kyi ming bri ba'am, yang na rde'u re la ming re bris te de dang de yin bsam, de thog ming mi gsal ba'i rde'u lnga drug sogs gang dgos bzhag ste
rows.english: If you want to be even more sure of who will be in the bounds of the retreat, then write out a physical list.  You can also take small stones and write each person's name on a different one, thinking "This stone is this person, and this stone is that."  Set aside as many stones as you might need, say five or six, without any specific name written on them.

rows.acip: RANG GI BLA MA ZHAL BZHUGS YOD MED GANG YIN YANG MTSAMS 'OG TU 'JOG ,PHA MA YANG NGES PAR 'JOG DGOS,

rows.english: Whether your own Lama is blessing this world with Their presence or not, you should include Them within the boundaries of the retreat.  You must absolutely do the same with your Father and Mother.
